newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egyptian police end search for militants in caves.
newsitem.headline: Egyptian police end search for militants in caves.

text.p: Police wound up a massive but largely fruitless seach for fugitive Islamist militants in southern Egypt on Saturday when they brought home the last of over 20 men who went missing during the 60-hour operation.

A helicopter flew the last three men, a captain and two other ranks, into the football stadium in the provincial capital Sohag, where they then received first aid for sunstroke. They were also hungry and thirsty, security sources said.
One unidentified man was killed in a gunbattle during the search, in which some 1,000 policemen trekked through the hills, but most of the militants apparently fled the area in advance.

The police were sweeping the hills and caves east of the Nile in Sohag province, about 400 km (250 miles) south of Cairo, in the belief that members of the militant Gama'a al-Islamiya (Islamic Group) were using the area as a base.

An Interior Ministry statement said police had cleared the caves and had found one 9mm pistol with ammunition, a four-kg (nine-lb) bomb packed in a jerrycan and mixed with ball bearings and an explosive booby trap fitted with springs.
About 60 of the policemen and their civilian auxiliaries suffered sunstroke or broken limbs. Security sources said 26 were missing on Friday but all have now been retrieved.

The Gama'a is the largest organisation fighting to overthrow the government and set up a strict Islamic state. More than 1,000 people have been killed in political violence in Egypt since the group took up arms in 1992.
Last month the police made a similar sweep of the hills in Assiut province further north.
The ministry said police were now planning similar operations along the edge of the eastern desert to clear it of militants and fugitive criminals.
